.. _X(381):

X(381) = MIDPOINT OF X(2) AND X(4)
==================================

.. figure:: x-00381.svg
   :alt: X(381) = MIDPOINT OF X(2) AND X(4)
   :align: center

   **X(381) = MIDPOINT OF X(2) AND X(4)** constructed on acute reference triangle :math:`(a, b, c) = (5, 6, 7)` with unit baseline :math:`AB = 1`.

Coordinates
-----------

Trilinears
~~~~~~~~~~

* :math:`2 \cos(B - C) - \cos A : :`
* :math:`\cos A + 4 \cos B \cos C : :`
* :math:`3 \cos A - 4 \sin B \sin C : :`
* :math:`(\csc A)(2 \tan A + \tan B + \tan C) + 2 \sec A : :`
* :math:`3 \cos B \cos C + \sin B \sin C : :`

Barycentrics
~~~~~~~~~~~~

* :math:`a(\cos A + 4 \cos B \cos C) : :`
* :math:`a^4 - 2b^4 - 2c^4 + a^2b^2 + a^2c^2 + 4b^2c^2 : :`
* :math:`S^2 + 3 SB SC : :`
* :math:`a^2*SA + 4*SB*SC : :`

* **Kimberling (6, 9, 13) Search Value:** :math:`-1.523625309219`

Notes
-----

.. container:: note-item

   As a point on the Euler line, :ref:`X(381) <X(381)>` has Shinagawa coefficients (1,3).

.. container:: note-item

   Let A' be the reflection of :ref:`X(3) <X(3)>` in A, and define B'and C' cyclically. Let A'' be the reflection of :ref:`X(3) <X(3)>` in BC, and define B'' and C'' cyclically. The lines A'A'', B'B'', C'C'' concur in :ref:`X(381) <X(381)>`.

.. container:: note-item

   :ref:`X(381) <X(381)>` is the point QA-P14 (Centroid of the Morley Triangle) of quadrangle ABC\ :ref:`X(2) <X(2)>` (see http://www.chrisvantienhoven.nl/quadrangle-objects/15-mathematics/quadrangle-objects/artikelen-qa/42-qa-p14.html)

.. container:: note-item

   Let Pa be the parabola with focus A and directrix BC. Let La be the polar of :ref:`X(3) <X(3)>` wrt Pa. Define Lb and Lc cyclically. Let A' = Lb∩Lc, B' = Lc∩La, C' = La∩Lb. The symmedian point of triangle A'B'C' is :ref:`X(381) <X(381)>`. Analogously, let La be the :term:`trilinear polar <trilinear-polar>` of A wrt BC\ :ref:`X(3) <X(3)>`, and define Lb and Lc cyclically. Let A'=Lb∩Lc, B'=Lc∩La, C'=La∩Lb. Equivalently, A'B'C' is the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :ref:`X(3) <X(3)>` wrt the cevian triangle of :ref:`X(3) <X(3)>`. Also, let A″ be the reflection of A' in BC, and define B″ and C″ cyclically. The lines AA″, BB″, CC″ concur in :ref:`X(381) <X(381)>`. Finally, let A' be the orthocenter of BC\ :ref:`X(6) <X(6)>`, and define B' and C' cyclically; then :ref:`X(381) <X(381)>` is the centroid of A'B'C'. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, September 5, 2015)

.. container:: note-item

   Let Sa be the similitude center of the orthocentroidal triangle and the A-altimedial triangle. Define Sb and Sc cyclically. The lines ASa, BSb, CSc concur in :ref:`X(381) <X(381)>`. (Randy Hutson, December 10, 2016)

.. container:: note-item

   Let A1B1C1 and A2B2C2 be the 1st and 2nd Ehrmann circumscribing triangles. Let A' be the :term:`crosspoint <crosspoint>` of A1 and A2, and define B', C' cyclically. The lines AA', BB', CC' concur in :ref:`X(381) <X(381)>`. (Randy Hutson, June 27, 2018)

Incidence
---------
